FITJMJjASUs.summary: Jim Weirich's RubyConf 2012 talk derives the Y combinator step by step, live-coding in Ruby lambdas. It builds up an understanding of functional programming and lambda calculus from first principles.
FITJMJjASUs.why: HN recommends it repeatedly as one of the best and most entertaining programming talks, and as the talk that makes the Y combinator click, even for people who do not use Ruby.

F_Riqjdh2oM.summary: An 88-minute Microsoft Research talk that explains how quantum computers beat classical ones using basic linear algebra, qubits, superposition and gates. It works through the Deutsch oracle problem and ends with entanglement, teleportation and a live demo.
F_Riqjdh2oM.why: It is HN's most frequently recommended starting point for quantum computing because it avoids pop-science hand-waving and needs only basic linear algebra.

Fy0aCDmgnxg.summary: Martin Jonasson and Petri Purho take a bland Breakout clone and add layer after layer of 'juice' such as easing, particles, screen shake and sound until it feels alive. A live demo makes the effect of small feedback details obvious.
Fy0aCDmgnxg.why: The go-to recommendation on game feel and polish, cited by HN as one of the best talks for anyone making interactive things feel good.

FACK2knC08E.summary: Hans Rosling uses data and animated statistics to show how world population is changing, why birth rates fall as child survival and wealth rise, and why population is expected to peak around 11 billion. It also tackles common misconceptions about Africa and family planning.
FACK2knC08E.why: HN repeatedly recommends it to counter overpopulation alarm with data on falling birth rates.

F-QA2rkpBSY.summary: Part 1 of a lecture by physicist Albert Bartlett on the exponential function and its consequences for population growth, resource use and energy. It argues that steady growth rates quickly lead to enormous quantities.
F-QA2rkpBSY.why: A perennial HN recommendation for building intuition about exponential growth, cited whenever endless growth, energy or population come up.

FvmTSpJU-Xc.summary: Alan Kay's 2009 UIUC talk arguing that computing is more a pop culture than a science and that ignoring history and fundamentals leads to inferior solutions. He touches on the history of interactive environments and what the web should have been.
FvmTSpJU-Xc.why: A staple on must-watch lists, recommended as a starting point for Kay's thinking and for why software is often poor and ahistorical.

F9cO3-MLHOM.summary: Bill Gurley's talk at the All-In Summit 2023, titled 2,851 Miles after the distance between Washington and San Francisco. He describes how incumbents use lobbying and regulation to entrench themselves, followed by a conversation with the hosts.
F9cO3-MLHOM.why: HN commenters repeatedly recommend it as the clearest explanation of regulatory capture, and cite it in threads on AI regulation, GDPR and telecom.

FJJTYQYB1JQ.summary: Andrei Alexandrescu's CppCon 2019 talk revisits sorting, showing how branchless tricks, hybrid strategies and a cost metric can speed up std::sort-style algorithms on modern hardware.
FJJTYQYB1JQ.why: HN recommends it as an entertaining talk that starts simple and goes deep on practical performance optimization.

FnEWBtCnFs8.summary: Jason Scott's DerbyCon 2012 talk on rescuing the Prince of Persia source code from old floppy disks, working with the game's author Jordan Mechner. It is a story of digital archaeology and recovering data from ancient media.
FnEWBtCnFs8.why: Repeatedly recommended as a favorite tech talk and a great example of digital preservation work.

FjHJ7FmV0M4.summary: A PBS clip in which Richard Feynman explains the strange nature of light and electromagnetic radiation. He conveys how little of it we actually see and how radio waves are present everywhere.
FjHJ7FmV0M4.why: Recommended as an entertaining, accessible way to get a feel for light and electric fields.

FssULNGSZIA.summary: Drummer Danny Carey performs Tool's 'Pneuma' live in Boston, in a Vic Firth session with close views of his playing.
FssULNGSZIA.why: HN commenters point to it as a showcase of astonishing drumming and music that gives chills.

FtieBc3KptU.summary: Science writer Jay Dixit explains how he uses Emacs as a non-programmer to write, edit and research more productively. He shows his plain-text writing workflow and what led him from tools like Scrivener to Emacs.
FtieBc3KptU.why: Recommended as a favorite talk showing Emacs as a writing environment rather than just a programmer's editor.

FvNRlE4E9QQ.summary: Jay Parlar's Strange Loop talk shows how model checkers such as Alloy can find complex bugs in a system's design without running or reading any code. He walks through modeling architectures and checking every possible sequence of operations, including a real security bug and a UI feature-interaction bug.
FvNRlE4E9QQ.why: HN commenters point to it as the best practical introduction to Alloy and to lightweight formal modeling.

F3ntGDm6hOs.summary: Day 1 of Handmade Hero's introduction to C on Windows, covering setting up Visual Studio, creating a Win32 project, the WinMain entry point and writing a first function. It is the starting point for Casey Muratori's from-scratch game series.
F3ntGDm6hOs.why: HN recommends it as an approachable way into C and low-level programming that gets to something visible quickly.

FF-tKLISfPE.summary: A clip from Steve Jobs's 1997 WWDC session, in which he answers a hostile question from an audience member about Apple killing OpenDoc. He says to start with the customer experience and work back to the technology, and that saying no is part of focus.
FF-tKLISfPE.why: Commenters link it as a canonical statement of Jobs's product philosophy and as an example of handling an insult calmly and articulately.

FihU5JxmnBg.summary: Stuart Halloway of Cognitect argues for debugging with the scientific method: form hypotheses, try to falsify them, and write everything down. The talk is given to the Clojure community but applies to any language.
FihU5JxmnBg.why: HN recommends it as a talk that changed how people debug, worth rewatching periodically.

FBaVwwuErmU.summary: The pilot of the British comedy series Look Around You, a deadpan parody of 1970s and 80s school science programmes, in which the scientists examine calcium.
FBaVwwuErmU.why: HN commenters recommend it as a surreal, perfectly observed parody of old educational films, and quote it in jokes.

FTKP0Y9MVus.summary: Captain Disillusion's comedic, fast-paced explainer on how color works in cameras, displays and video. It covers the biology of color perception and what it means for screens.
FTKP0Y9MVus.why: Commenters recommend it as a dense but entertaining primer on color theory and color in video systems.

FfDa8tR25dk.summary: A Ukrainian documentary about the liquidators who cleaned radioactive debris off the Chernobyl reactor roof in two-minute shifts. It presents their firsthand accounts and footage of the work.
FfDa8tR25dk.why: Recommended as a moving, first-person account of the people who dealt with the worst of the Chernobyl cleanup.

F8sZRBdmqc0.summary: Bryan Cantrill presents the ARC (Adaptive Replacement Cache) paper by Megiddo and Modha at Papers We Love. He opens with a survey of caching strategies before digging into the self-tuning LRU/MFU design.
F8sZRBdmqc0.why: Recommended in cache-algorithm threads as a fun, informative walk through caching strategies and ARC.

FKTxC9pl-WM.summary: Kathy Sierra's Fluent 2015 keynote on the one metaskill for developers: the ability to come up to speed quickly and stay there. She covers how people learn, cognitive resources versus willpower, and building skill.
FKTxC9pl-WM.why: HN commenters recommend it when asked how to learn better or keep improving.

FjA0EQPeUGM.summary: A 1973 NBC News documentary on the US nerve gas arsenal, covering leaks in Okinawa, a Utah test that killed thousands of sheep, and the long-term hazards of storage sites. It won an Emmy.
FjA0EQPeUGM.why: HN commenters recommend it as a fascinating, Emmy-winning look at US chemical weapons stockpiles and their dangers.

FxKtZmQgxrI.summary: The first of seven parts of RedLetterMedia's long review of Star Wars: The Phantom Menace. It argues that the film's central flaw is its characters and the lack of audience connection.
FxKtZmQgxrI.why: HN commenters recommend it as sharp film criticism and a lesson in filmmaking, and cite it when arguing the prequels failed on basics.

F3Jd9GI6XqE.summary: Lex Fridman interviews MIT psycholinguist Edward Gibson on human language, syntax, grammar and how large language models relate to them. The conversation runs nearly three hours.
F3Jd9GI6XqE.why: HN cites it for the argument that LLMs capture language form but not meaning, and for how the brain's language network works.

F_7S1eqKsFk.summary: Theo de Raadt presents pledge, a new OpenBSD security mechanism that kills processes which exceed the system calls they declared they need. The talk was given late at night at Hackfest 2015.
F_7S1eqKsFk.why: HN points to it as the canonical overview of pledge and the ideas behind OpenBSD's exploit mitigations.

Fgh2dFngFsg.summary: Aaron Swartz's keynote at Freedom to Connect 2012 describing how ordinary people helped defeat the SOPA censorship bill. He recounts how the Senate unexpectedly united behind the bill and how grassroots action stopped it.
Fgh2dFngFsg.why: HN shares it as an inspiring account of citizens changing Washington, especially after Swartz's death.

FkKPsLxgpuY.summary: Veritasium takes an IQ test and examines what IQ measures, its history including military use and eugenics, its controversies, and how it correlates with life outcomes. Experts including Cecil Reynolds and Stuart Ritchie contribute.
FkKPsLxgpuY.why: Recommended as a good primer on what IQ scores mean and their limited effect on life outcomes.

F-yDKeya4SU.summary: Engineering Explained examines new research suggesting corn ethanol in US gasoline may emit as much or more carbon than gasoline. It covers the Renewable Fuel Standard and why ethanol was assumed to be a green fuel.
F-yDKeya4SU.why: Cited as an accessible summary of evidence that corn ethanol is no better than gasoline for emissions.

F04dGK1_wYA.summary: Fred Dibnah, the English steeplejack, shows how ladders are fixed up the outside of a tall brick mill chimney. The footage was filmed in the mid-1990s and is part one of two.
F04dGK1_wYA.why: People point to it as a vivid explanation of how industrial chimneys were climbed for inspection and repair.

F1Hq8eVOMHs.summary: A Kurzgesagt animated explainer on the climate and environmental cost of meat. It covers how beef drives deforestation and emissions, and how this compares with plant-based foods.
F1Hq8eVOMHs.why: HN commenters cite it as a clear, well-sourced summary of why meat, especially beef, has such a large environmental footprint.

F8JCh0owT4w.summary: A Motherboard documentary episode from Nebraska about farmers and mechanics fighting manufacturers like John Deere over access to the diagnostic software needed to repair modern tractors. It shows how software locks have taken away farmers' traditional self-reliance.
F8JCh0owT4w.why: Offered as a concrete, human example in right-to-repair discussions of how software lock-in affects expensive equipment.

FBsP-bmDLOo.summary: Physicist Sabine Hossenfelder explains how 5G works and examines the health concerns around millimeter wave radiation. She reviews the scientific evidence and the open letters from scientists.
FBsP-bmDLOo.why: HN recommends it as an even-handed physicist's take for 5G skeptics, noting it is probably safe but under-studied.

FH2WeWgcSMk.summary: The first of three short films by Mike Nayna about Bret Weinstein and Heather Heying's experience at Evergreen State College, focusing on the Equity Council and the controversy around it.
FH2WeWgcSMk.why: HN commenters cite the series as a documentary on the Evergreen controversy and as evidence in arguments about ideology and campus culture.

FV0DXNB94NE.summary: Richard Feldman describes introducing Elm into a mixed React and jQuery front-end in production, and why the result was reliable, clean and fast enough to make the back-end team jealous.
FV0DXNB94NE.why: HN people recommend it as a quick way to get a sense of what Elm does and what adopting it incrementally looks like.

FV8n_E_6Tpc.summary: Cindy Gallop gives a 4-minute TED2009 talk arguing hardcore pornography has distorted how young men think about sex. She introduces her website MakeLoveNotPorn as a response.
FV8n_E_6Tpc.why: HN people share it as a short, frank talk about porn versus real-life sex expectations.

FegjLbCnoBw.summary: Dave Chinner's linux.conf.au 2012 talk on XFS scalability, covering pain points with large numbers of files and complex metadata, and the work to fix XFS metadata performance.
FegjLbCnoBw.why: HN recommends it as the definitive explanation of XFS metadata performance fixes and how XFS was developed and made robust on Linux.

FlQYU3m1e80.summary: Scott Manley explains the thermal balance of spacecraft and how a satellite could be configured to radiate away the heat from datacenter-scale computing in space. His rough numbers suggest it is feasible.
FlQYU3m1e80.why: HN points to it as a convincing energy-budget analysis in debates over space datacenters, while debating its assumptions.

FquNpWdf9vg.summary: A 1987 episode of The Computer Chronicles on Apple's HyperCard, showing users building their own applications. Gary Kildall appears and Bill Atkinson discusses the program, with credit given to earlier influences.
FquNpWdf9vg.why: HN points to it as a period view of HyperCard and a source for its history and influences.

FyKRubB5N60.summary: Part one of Technology Connections' account of the VHS versus Betamax format war. It argues Sony was caught off guard by JVC's cheaper, more practical VHS system.
FyKRubB5N60.why: HN recommends it as a detailed, accurate explanation of why Betamax lost, and cites it in debates over whether VHS was actually the worse format.

FzF1KySHmUA.summary: A short video from a blacksmith, who heats and bends steel to rebut the claim that jet fuel could not weaken the steel in the World Trade Center. It is delivered with a lot of attitude.
FzF1KySHmUA.why: HN commenters use it as a quick, hands-on demonstration that steel loses strength well below its melting point.

FzRP1qdwPKw.summary: Dave Jones of EEVblog and Richard Stephenson tour the 70m DSS43 dish at the Canberra Deep Space Communication Complex and explain how NASA talks to Voyager 2. It covers the transmitters, receivers and tracking involved.
FzRP1qdwPKw.why: Recommended in Voyager threads as the best look at how operators actually contact the probe.

Fzmm87oVQ6c.summary: Hamish Coleman describes reverse engineering the keyboard controller in a Thinkpad and reflashing it with custom firmware. He covers how Lenovo secures its firmware, and his ongoing work on the protocol between the BIOS and the vendor flash tool.
Fzmm87oVQ6c.why: HN people cite it as an approachable, hands-on introduction to hardware and firmware reverse engineering, and as the author's own account of the Thinkpad keyboard patch effort.

F6FR08VylO4.summary: Sean Carroll's Talks at Google presentation of his book Something Deeply Hidden. He gives an accessible introduction to quantum mechanics and argues for the many-worlds interpretation and the emergence of spacetime.
F6FR08VylO4.why: Recommended as an approachable case that the Everett (many-worlds) interpretation is the simplest reading of quantum mechanics.

FUPstXCqyus.summary: MC Frontalot's nerdcore song "Secrets From The Future" (2007), about secrets not staying hidden once future technology can break today's encryption.
FUPstXCqyus.why: Brought up in threads on encryption and quantum cracking as a fitting song about future decryption.

FaAZAII2x0w.summary: Google's Amin Vahdat gives the ONS 2015 keynote on Google's datacenter networking, including its custom hardware, software-defined networking and very high bisection bandwidth.
FaAZAII2x0w.why: HN cites it as a rare public look at Google's internal network design and how it scales to many VMs.

FhL5VO2NStU.summary: A 2006 Google Tech Talk by Robert Bussard on inertial electrostatic confinement (polywell) fusion as a cheap, clean alternative to conventional thermonuclear reactors. He argues it could be made viable with modest funding.
FhL5VO2NStU.why: Cited as Bussard's last substantial public presentation on polywell fusion and the source of his claim that about $200M would be enough.

F0_q-fD_lyU.summary: The Thought Emporium shows how easily bacteria can be genetically modified to produce fluorescent proteins and even bioluminesce, with techniques doable at home. It links to companion videos on incubators, DNA extraction and gels.
F0_q-fD_lyU.why: HN points to it as proof that DIY genetic engineering is feasible and as an example of a rigorous hands-on biology channel.

F3FkAUbetWU.summary: Destin Sandlin of Smarter Every Day fires .22 Magnum and .38 Special bullets at Prince Rupert's drops, filmed at 170,000 frames per second. The slow-motion footage shows the bullet shattering against the glass tadpole while the drop initially survives.
F3FkAUbetWU.why: Cited in Prince Rupert's drop threads as the best high-speed footage of a bullet hitting one.

FBOLk9s9Ci4.summary: YC partner Michael Seibel discusses his essay on real product-market fit, why founders wrongly believe they have it, and how building a company is not a single-variable problem, drawing on Justin.tv and Socialcam.
FBOLk9s9Ci4.why: HN points founders to YC's content like this for practical startup advice on product-market fit.

FBeSKL9zVro.summary: BigClive explains why microwave oven transformer projects are extremely dangerous, since the high voltage and high current can kill. He contrasts them with spot welder builds where the secondary is replaced by low-voltage heavy wire.
FBeSKL9zVro.why: HN points to it as the authoritative explanation of why fractal wood burning with MOTs is deadly and how to reduce the risk.

FKXOucXB4a8.summary: MIT researchers show that sound can be recovered from silent video by analyzing tiny vibrations in objects such as a potato chip bag. It works even with consumer cameras by using rolling shutter.
FKXOucXB4a8.why: HN commenters cite it as the classic demonstration of audio recovery from video in surveillance and privacy discussions.

FN2RM-CHkuI.summary: A family comedy video in which kids write instructions for making a peanut butter and jelly sandwich, and a parent follows them with exact literalness, producing chaos. This is the classroom-friendly version.
FN2RM-CHkuI.why: HN uses it as shorthand for how hard it is to write unambiguous instructions, in discussions of programming, tutorials and LLM prompting.

FY_NtO7SIrY.summary: Destin Sandlin of Smarter Every Day investigates manipulation on Facebook, interviewing the company's team about content moderation. It is the third video in his series on social media manipulation.
FY_NtO7SIrY.why: HN commenters cite it for numbers on Facebook's moderation scale and for Destin's ability to get platforms to speak openly about manipulation.

F_sbusEUz5w.summary: Google I/O 2011 session by Ray Cromwell and Philip Rogers on writing 2D and 3D games with HTML5 and GWT. It covers porting game libraries and physics engines, sharing code with Android, and publishing to the Chrome Web Store, and showcases the ForPlay library.
F_sbusEUz5w.why: HN cites it as the original showing of ForPlay (later PlayN), the cross-platform Java game library.

FeAMiBKi_EM.summary: A ten-minute clip from Jonathan Blow's talk on preventing the collapse of civilization, arguing that software quality and the knowledge to build it are in decline.
FeAMiBKi_EM.why: Pulled out in threads about declining software quality, though some commenters distrust Blow's claims about game and web development.

FinRqCocwGE.summary: A VICE report from 2011 in which Suroosh Alvi revisits the gun markets in Pakistan's tribal areas, a stronghold of the Taliban. It shows weapons being made and sold by hand and a country described as a powder keg.
FinRqCocwGE.why: HN uses it as a visual reference for hand-built firearms and craft gunsmithing, especially in threads on 3D-printed and home-made guns.

Fiu9GSOmt8E.summary: John Oliver explains how plastics harm the planet and why recycling is not the solution consumers have been led to believe. He argues corporations and policymakers must act, not just individuals.
Fiu9GSOmt8E.why: HN cites it as a clear explanation of how industry shifted recycling responsibility onto consumers and why most plastic isn't recycled.

FlApbxLz6pA.summary: A short BicycleDutch episode showing how Dutch protected intersections continue cycle paths through the junction without needing extra street width.
FlApbxLz6pA.why: HN uses it as the standard reference for how the Netherlands solves cyclist and driver conflicts at intersections.

FyK4P7ZdOK8.summary: Andreas Antonopoulos argues that money has a fourth function beyond store of value, medium of exchange and unit of account, which is as a system of control. He covers the history of money and why it does not flow freely.
FyK4P7ZdOK8.why: Cited in discussions of cryptocurrency, KYC/AML and financial surveillance as a framing of money as a tool of control.

F3rrjQtQe5A.summary: A run through the 32 factory presets of the Yamaha DX7 FM synthesizer, with timestamps for each patch such as brass, strings, pianos, bass and tubular bells. It is a straight audio demo of the sounds.
F3rrjQtQe5A.why: HN uses it as a reference for how DX7 patches and FM synthesis actually sound.

F4CX-9lkRMQ.summary: Additional camera angles of the 1988 Sandia National Laboratories rocket-sled test in which an F-4 Phantom was crashed at about 500 mph into a block of reinforced concrete. The footage shows the aircraft disintegrating against the wall.
F4CX-9lkRMQ.why: HN commenters cite it in nuclear and engineering debates as evidence that concrete containment structures can withstand aircraft impacts.

F4IGl4OizM4.summary: A short Boeing-supplied clip where the 737 MAX program's chief project engineer explains how the lengthened landing gear of the MAX 10 folds up. It shows the gear model in motion.
F4IGl4OizM4.why: Used as a concrete illustration of the commonality constraints that forced Boeing's 737 MAX design choices.

F7SNEdjftno.summary: A short clip from the 1999 film Office Space in which Joanna quits her restaurant job with flair after her boss's demands. It is a comic scene about disaffected workers.
F7SNEdjftno.why: HN uses it as a joke reference in threads about quiet quitting and unreasonable workplace demands.

F7pYHN9iC9I.summary: A Belgian bank-safety campaign video in which a supposed clairvoyant stuns people by revealing personal financial details, then shows he found them all online. It warns viewers to be careful about what they share and about online banking security.
F7pYHN9iC9I.why: Cited as a vivid demonstration of how much personal data is findable and shared online, in privacy and tracking threads.

F9t3FREAZ-k.summary: An early 2009 tech test by Notch of an Infiniminer-style cave game running about 700 fps on a 256x256x64 tile map. It is the prototype that grew into Minecraft.
F9t3FREAZ-k.why: HN links it as a historical artifact showing what Minecraft looked like at its very beginning.

FADQAnq0RpA.summary: Chris McCord's ElixirConf EU 2023 keynote tracing LiveView's evolution from simple form validation to full apps, with code examples and live demos of what 1.0 will offer.
FADQAnq0RpA.why: Referenced as a demo of how easily Phoenix LiveView handles things like bidirectional infinite pagination with streams.

FHwnrYm0mNc.summary: A DevOps YouTuber tests GitHub Copilot on a range of Leetcode problems and finds it solves most immediately, with a few needing tweaks and some far off. He concludes it would outperform him in a FAANG-style interview.
FHwnrYm0mNc.why: Cited as evidence that AI can solve interview-style algorithm puzzles, in threads questioning the value of Leetcode.

FKCmyiljKo0.summary: The famous 'I'm Spartacus' scene from the 1960 film, in which every slave stands up to claim to be Spartacus to protect him from the Romans.
FKCmyiljKo0.why: Used as a pop-culture reference, usually as a joke about everyone sharing the same identity or name.

FL5U4wr86L4.summary: Scott Long of Netflix presents the architecture of the OpenConnect content delivery network at NYCBSDCon 2014. He explains why Netflix runs FreeBSD 10 on its appliances and what the future holds.
FL5U4wr86L4.why: Cited as the primary source for why Netflix uses FreeBSD and UFS rather than ZFS on its CDN boxes, and for its GPL reasoning.

FL7yD-0pqZg.summary: A short xtranormal-animated comedy sketch comparing the iPhone 4 and the HTC Evo. It dates from the 2010 smartphone wars.
FL7yD-0pqZg.why: Only posted as a joke in threads about iPhone versus Android; no one recommends it for content.

FQrEDq8KPiU.summary: An Asianometry documentary-style video on the rise and collapse of China's dockless bike-share boom. It covers the startups, the heavy subsidies and the price wars.
FQrEDq8KPiU.why: HN cites it as an analogy for loss-leader pricing and market-share wars, for example in AI pricing.

FVbEoZXhCrM.summary: A one-minute Yahoo Finance clip of President Biden saying he would shut down the Nord Stream 2 pipeline if Russia further invaded Ukraine.
FVbEoZXhCrM.why: HN commenters cite it as evidence in arguments over who was behind the Nord Stream sabotage, quoting Biden's statement.

FXe1hBvlylw.summary: Fully Charged host Robert Llewellyn visits Orkney, where wind, tidal, wave and solar generation plus community energy schemes power the islands. It presents the archipelago as a model for future energy systems.
FXe1hBvlylw.why: Cited as an example of Orkney's grid innovation and role as a test site for renewable tech.

FY7DtKMBxBw.summary: Hugh Jeffreys tears down the iPhone 12 and assesses its repairability, focusing on how parts are serialized and tied to the device so swapping components between phones does not work.
FY7DtKMBxBw.why: HN cites it as evidence of Apple's parts-pairing restrictions in right-to-repair discussions.

FY8SwIvxj8o.summary: Sir Mashalot blends six formulaic pop country songs into one seamless mashup using Pro Tools. It shows how similar the songs' chords and structure are.
FY8SwIvxj8o.why: Cited as a demonstration of how samey pop music is, in threads about chord progressions and homogeneous music.

FYJ1dbyDcrI.summary: A short Tim and Eric Awesome Show sketch, The Universe I, II & III, in which the cosmos is shown in a deliberately absurd way. It is an Adult Swim surreal comedy bit.
FYJ1dbyDcrI.why: HN uses it as a mind-blown reaction clip in threads about physics, space and GIFs.

FYdAT0v4DHs.summary: Scott Manley tells the story of a computerized telemetry system built to sit at the heart of a nuclear test device in place of the plutonium pit, designed to transmit data in the microseconds before it was destroyed.
FYdAT0v4DHs.why: HN mentions it only in passing, as a reference for instrumented dummy warheads and implosion-test data in nuclear-testing threads.

FZ6lZJWL_Xk.summary: Tesla's 2014 event where Elon Musk unveiled the dual motor all-wheel-drive Model S and the first Autopilot features.
FZ6lZJWL_Xk.why: Mostly cited as a primary source for what Tesla and Musk said about Autopilot and automatic charging at the time.

FZi9CSB9_kk.summary: A DConf 2019 talk by Robert Schadek arguing that spreadsheets are the world's dominant programming language and that D can be used to replace them. It looks at spreadsheet quirks and then at techniques for moving away from them.
FZi9CSB9_kk.why: Mostly appears as a link in Who is hiring job posts from a company using D, and once as deeper background in a thread about Excel.

F_7IPm7f1vI.summary: Boston Dynamics shows the electric Atlas autonomously moving engine covers between containers and a sequencing dolly. It uses an ML vision model and grasping policy with no teleoperation or prescribed motions.
F_7IPm7f1vI.why: Used as a data point on how capable humanoid robots are at practical tasks, with commenters noting how far they are from household chores.

FaOSCASqLsE.summary: An SNL sketch in which Kylo Ren goes undercover as a radar technician named Matt at Starkiller Base, parodying the show Undercover Boss.
FaOSCASqLsE.why: HN commenters mostly invoke it as a joke when discussing meetings, management and workplace absurdity.

FbZ-chrOgGg.summary: Intro and gameplay footage of Rescue on Fractalus, the 1985 Lucasfilm Games title for Atari XL/XE, programmed by Loren Carpenter and David Fox. It shows the game's fractal-generated mountain terrain.
FbZ-chrOgGg.why: Shown as a historic example of fractal terrain rendering in games, in threads about voxel and terrain rendering.

FcW9kUUTfxY.summary: A short test firing of the XRS-2200 linear aerospike engine at NASA Stennis Space Center, which was designed for the cancelled X-33 VentureStar. The engine is shown at roughly 80 percent of max thrust.
FcW9kUUTfxY.why: Linked as the go-to footage of a linear aerospike engine actually running whenever aerospike nozzles come up.

Fd-_VDYit3U.summary: A five-minute C-SPAN clip of Dr. Jared Cooney Horvath testifying to a US Senate committee that screen time, including in schools, harms children's learning and cognitive development.
Fd-_VDYit3U.why: HN commenters link it as a concise piece of expert testimony in threads on declining test scores and technology in education.

Fdd6sQ8Cbe0.summary: A short 2009 WIRED clip showing Kiva Systems robots moving inventory shelves in a warehouse serving online retailer Zappos. It shows how mobile robots bring goods to pickers instead of people walking the aisles.
Fdd6sQ8Cbe0.why: HN commenters link it as a concrete picture of Kiva-style robotic warehouses whenever threads discuss warehouse automation and same-day delivery.

FeSCEalMOL8.summary: A short CNBC report on Zipline, which has delivered medical supplies by drone in Rwanda since 2016 and is preparing to start in the U.S.
FeSCEalMOL8.why: HN cites Zipline as an example of a drone company doing meaningful work with a fixed-base delivery approach.

FfJv9QYrlwg.summary: A short Bloomberg clip from the 2018 UN General Assembly. Trump warns that Germany will become dependent on Russian energy, and German delegates are shown reacting with laughter.
FfJv9QYrlwg.why: Cited in 2022 energy-crisis threads, mostly critically, as proof that Germany was warned about Russian gas dependence.

Fgcd1ghag5Y.summary: A short clip of Hillary Clinton reacting to news of Muammar Gaddafi's death with 'We came, we saw, he died', as reposted by a news channel.
Fgcd1ghag5Y.why: Cited critically in political threads about US foreign policy and Libya.

Fh_UDQnboRw.summary: A short clip of Bill Gates demonstrating Visual Basic in 1991, showing drag-and-drop building of a Windows GUI.
Fh_UDQnboRw.why: HN cites it as an example of rapid GUI development that modern tooling hasn't matched, and as precedent for promises of coding without developers.

FiCqlYKRlAA.summary: GameSpot meets the VP of Senseg, a company adding electrostatic touch feedback to tablets and touch surfaces, and demonstrates the technology.

FmXLqImT1wE.summary: A circa-1964 film showing AMF's AMFare system, which ordered, cooked and packaged hamburgers, fries, shakes and more automatically for a pilot fast-food operation.

Fow7iUaKrq4.summary: Raw footage of nerdcore rapper Monzy performing outside Stanford's computer science building, shot for the documentary Nerdcore for Life. The set includes his song about the kill -9 Unix command.

Fpu5a0Bl8eY.summary: The official HD music video for NENA's 1983 hit 99 Luftballons, a Cold War song about balloons triggering a war.

FzDBiUemCSY.summary: A short clip of a young Steve Jobs preparing for an early TV appearance, amazed to see himself on a nearby monitor. It includes the moment when a large white earpiece is put in his ear.
